title: Supervised learning needs labels
text:
Supervised learning needs labels
• Classic recipe: many pairs (x, y) →train end-to-end
• Works when labels are cheap and cover the domain
Reality
Labels are often expensive, slow, or noisy — unlabeled x is cheap.

title: Pretext task
text:
Pretext task
Definition
A pretext task is a problem we design so that solving it forces the encoder to
capture useful structure in x.
• Target is computed automatically from x
• Examples: reconstruct, predict rotation, match two views

title: Pretext head
text:
Pretext head
• Small network on top of h (classifier, decoder, projector, . . . )
• Exists to define the loss during pretraining
• Usually thrown away before the real task
• If a projector is used: h →g →z (loss on z; keep h)

title: How to choose (rules of thumb)
text:
How to choose (rules of thumb)
• Want simple first demo →reconstruction / rotation
• Want strong vision features →SimCLR, then DINO / MAE
• Want language / sequence models →next-token or masked LM
• Want “fill in the blank” (vision) →masked / MAE-style

SimCLR (contrastive SSL)
• Encoder f : backbone that maps a view →representation h (kept for
downstream)
• Projector g: small MLP h →z used only to compute the contrastive
loss (discarded later)
• NT-Xent loss: Normalized Temperature-scaled Cross-Entropy — pull
two views of the same x; push other views in the batch

• Forces the model to capture syntax, semantics, long context

text:

for x in unlabeled_loader:

loss = nt_xent(z1, z2, tau)
loss.backward(); opt.step()
# later: discard projector; train task head on encoder(h)

title: What to remember
text:
What to remember
• SSL learns an encoder fθ from data without task labels
• The supervision signal is created from the data itself
• Encoder representation h is the reusable asset
• Basic paradigms: reconstruction, predictive, contrastive
• Also: self-distillation, masked prediction, autoregressive prediction
• Downstream: linear probe or fine-tune
• Transformer later: a powerful backbone for several of these objectives

What to remember
• SSL learns an encoder fθ from data without task labels
• The supervision signal is created from the data itself
• Encoder representation h is the reusable asset
• Basic paradigms: reconstruction, predictive, contrastive
• Also: self-distillation, masked prediction, autoregressive prediction
• Downstream: linear probe or fine-tune
• Transformer later: a powerful backbone for several of these objectives
